title: Velasco Meets With Marco Rubio in Washington; They Address Issues Focused on Migration and Fentanyl
author: Arturo Sánchez Jiménez
content:
_This article by[Arturo Sánchez
Jiménez](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Arturo%20S%C3%A1nchez%20Jim%C3%A9nez)
originally appeared in the [August 26, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/08/26/politica/velasco-se-
reune-con-marco-rubio-en-washington-abordan-temas-orientados-a-migracion-y-
fentanilo), Mexico's premier left-wing daily newspaper._

**Washington**. Foreign Secretary Roberto Velasco met on the morning of this
Wednesday in Washington with United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

After the meeting, Rubio posted on the social network X: **" Met with Mexican
Foreign Secretary @r_velascoa to discuss decisive actions to end illegal
immigration, halt fentanyl trafficking, and dismantle Foreign Terrorist
Organizations and cartels."**

> Met with Mexican Foreign Secretary @r_velascoa to discuss decisive actions
> to end illegal immigration, halt fentanyl trafficking, and dismantle Foreign
> Terrorist Organizations and cartels.
>
> -- Secretary Marco Rubio (@SecRubio) [August 26,
> 2026](https://twitter.com/SecRubio/status/2092666734423552071?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

According to a statement from the Secretariat of Foreign Relations (SRE), in
the meeting both secretaries highlighted the progress on security in the
region, particularly in combating the trafficking of drugs and weapons and
transnational organized crime.

Velasco reiterated, according to the department, the importance of continuing
bilateral collaboration based on respect for sovereignty, shared
responsibility, mutual trust, and collaboration without subordination.

The foreign ministry also specified that the two officials addressed the
progress on irregular migration and continued the dialogue on the protection
of the human rights of Mexican people during migratory processes in the United
States.

> COMUNICADO. "Reunión entre el secretario de Relaciones Exteriores, Roberto
> Velasco Álvarez, y el secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio".  
>  
> <https://t.co/w6bDajqdg2>
>
> -- Relaciones Exteriores (@SRE_mx) [August 26,
> 2026](https://twitter.com/SRE_mx/status/2092670295198908643?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Velasco had announced the meeting on Tuesday, also through X, where he wrote
that, "after two very productive days in Seoul," he was landing in Washington
to hold "various meetings on priority issues of the bilateral agenda,"
beginning with his meeting with the Secretary of State.

> Tras dos días muy productivos en Seúl, República de Corea, aterrizo en
> Washington D. C. Mañana sostendré diversas reuniones sobre temas
> prioritarios de la agenda bilateral, comenzando con mi homólogo, el
> secretario de Estado Marco Rubio.
>
> -- Roberto Velasco Álvarez (@r_velascoa) [August 25,
> 2026](https://twitter.com/r_velascoa/status/2092435020648517653?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

## Velasco-Rubio Meeting Occurs Amid Bilateral Tension Over Handover of
Officials and Tariff Negotiation

The meeting between the two foreign ministers occurs at a time when the US
government is asking Mexico to hand over 10 officials and former officials
flagged by United States justice for alleged ties to the Los Chapitos faction
of the Sinaloa Cartel, among them the governor of Sinaloa on leave, Rubén
Rocha Moya.

The meeting also coincides with the visit to Washington of Economy Secretary
Marcelo Ebrard, who is negotiating with the US administration an agreement to
avoid the imposition of more tariffs on Mexican products. President Claudia
Sheinbaum expressed on Monday her optimism that this agreement could be
reached this very week.

Velasco was accompanied at the meeting by:

  * Ambassador Roberto Lazzeri Montaño
  * The Undersecretary for North America, Cristina Planter Riebeling
  * The head of the Unit for the Projection of Diplomacy, Foreign Policy, and Interinstitutional Organization, Efraín Guadarrama Pérez
  * The chief of staff to Ambassador Lazzeri, Carlos Botello
  * The director general of Special Affairs and Border Modernization, Oliver Arroyo Ramón
  * The head of Border and Special Affairs, Rafael Saucedo Fuentes
